methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Growth → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $1.7B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 8 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Atoms, a Growth-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Travis Kalanick, has raised $1.7B to date. The valuation analysis draws from a sector universe of 9 peers—1 public (ticker 277810.KQ) and 8 private companies including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Bedrock Robotics, and Dexterity—though a sufficiently narrow peer cohort at identical stage and valuation tier does not exist to support a robust median-based valuation.

The Stage-Progression method is the primary applicable approach here. Using total capital raised of $1.7B as a proxy baseline and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical for Growth-stage progression yields $2.0B. This method assumes incremental valuation expansion consistent with the company's stage transition, though without comparable recent financings in the immediate peer set, the multiplier carries model risk.

The triangulated valuation range is $1.7B (low) to $2.3B (median $2.0B), derived from a single methodology. The low bound reflects the raised capital itself; the high bound applies upside sensitivity. Key uncertainties include the absence of contemporaneous comparables at identical stage and scale, limiting confidence in the step-up multiplier, and the reliance on a single method. A secondary valuation approach anchored to either sector median revenue multiples or recent private market transactions in robotics would materially strengthen conviction in this range.
